From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@stratavault.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive price match: onboarding credit split & runtime packaging questions

Hi Sam,

Great meeting yesterday — appreciate the candid notes on where StrataVault is leaning. On our side I ran the numbers and attached a more explicit pricing_grid_v2.xlsx that shows a few ways we can structure a match to your incumbent while keeping predictable unit economics for production.

Quick summary (see sheet):
- Option A (Seat-first): seat-based core bundle + token overage; 20% migration credit applied as upfront credit over 3 months.
- Option B (Token-first): token-committed discount with onboarding credit applied as paydown on first two invoices.
- Tech add-ons: KV cache reserved slots and prefetched KV bucket to reduce peak token load (saves ~15% on peak cost in our perf model).

A couple of questions from Procurement we want to pre-answer:
- Would credits be refundable if go-live slips >90 days? We typically amortize credits but can make a milestone tie to go-live.
- Does the seat cap allow burst-only tokens? Yes — we can put a soft cap with bursts billed as overage at a pre-agreed rate.

Can you confirm the incumbent's effective unit price ($/k token) and any contract termination timing? If you can share the procurement contact (CC'd is fine), we'll prepare a formal counter with an execution-ready SOW.

If helpful, we can do a 30-min review Monday to walk the grid and the KV-cache impact numbers.

Thanks —
Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0184
redwood.com

Connor —

Thanks for the file. A few clarifications from my side (Procurement is looped):

1) Incumbent effective price: roughly $0.0085 / 1k tokens tiered; current contract renewal window is late Nov (30 days notice).
2) Onboarding credit: need clarity whether that credit is strictly for services (SOW) or can be applied to run-rate invoices. Prefer run-rate credits applied over first 60 days.
3) Seat vs token: we want a model that caps headcount exposure (seat cap) but allows predictable burst. Are you proposing reserved KV cache as part of the seat bundle? If so, what's the delta on the monthly charge?
4) Audit & SLAs: need confirmation that any cheaper model variants still meet 99.9% latency SLO for our primary region (us-west).

Also cc'ing Procurement lead (procure@stratavault.com) who will own the legal and termination questions.

Appreciate a short write-up we can take to the commercial committee.

— Sam
VP, Product — StrataVault
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: StrataVault pricing clarifications — need recommendation

Marissa / Lauren —

Forwarding Sam's replies. Key asks: apply onboarding credit to run-rate (first 60 days), seat cap with burst tokens, KV cache sizing + price delta, and SLA confirmation for us-west 99.9%. Procurement's renewal window is late Nov so timing is tight (need signed by early Nov to avoid automatic renewal).

My proposed counter (numbers on the attached SOW-draft.pdf):
- Commercial: 18-month term, commit to 6M tokens/month base; seat-based admin bundle (up to 25 seats) included; token overage at $0.0092 / 1k (tiered down after 12M).
- Migration/onboarding: 18% migration credit (~$60k) applied as a run-rate credit over first 3 invoices (60/30/10 split by invoice).
- KV cache: include 64 reserved KV slots in seat bundle; additional KV capacity $1,200 / reserved unit / month. Based on their perf profile this yields ~12–16% per-token cost reduction at peak.
- SLA: 99.9% regional latency SLO guaranteed; fallbacks to verified model variant if hardware constrained (documented in SOW).

Trade-offs and options to preserve margin: convert migration credit from percent to fixed dollar if legal asks for stricter auditability. Also can shorten credit window to 2 invoices if they push back.

Please review SOW-draft.pdf and pricing_grid_v2.xlsx; flags and alternate phrasing by EOD and I will send the counter next business day.

— Connor

Connor —

Quick read — I like the 18% credit but recommend we tighten the milestone language: tie 50% of the credit to production go-live (successful routing, latency tests, and basic eval pass) and the remainder amortized over the first two invoices. That reduces risk if they stall.

On KV pricing, $1,200 / reserved unit is acceptable if we cap additional capacity increases to 20% without renegotiation. For SLA language, explicitly call out failover to a verified smaller-quant model (quantized variant) with known latency characteristics and include a 30-day rollback window.

If Procurement insists on credits applied only to SOW vs run-rate, offer a blended option: 10% applied to SOW, 8% as run-rate credit. That gives them bookkeeping flexibility while keeping cash flow visible to us.

Happy to join the call Monday to present.

— Marissa
Director, Commercial Strategy

Sam / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clarifications and for looping Procurement. Per our internal review we've prepared a formal counter and an execution-ready SOW attached. Highlights below (a concise table is in the attachment):

1) Commercial terms
- Term: 18 months
- Base commit: 6,000,000 tokens / month
- Price: $0.0092 / 1k tokens on overage; effective blended price at commit = $0.0079 / 1k tokens
- Seat bundle: up to 25 named seats included (admin, engineering, monitoring).

2) Migration / onboarding credit (your preference honored)
- Blended option: 10% of migration estimate applied to SOW items (professional services), 8% applied as run-rate credit across the first two invoices. Total effective credit = 18% (~$60k).
- Milestone: 50% of run-rate credit contingent on production go-live within 90 days; remainder applied to invoice schedule.

3) KV cache & runtime packaging
- Included: 64 reserved KV slots in seat bundle.
- Additional reserved KV: $1,200 / unit / month, capped at 20% growth in the first year without renegotiation.
- Performance note: our bench indicates a 12–16% reduction in peak token consumption with this KV reservation and prefix caching strategies — included in Appendix A.

4) SLA & fallback
- 99.9% latency SLO (us-west).
- If hardware constraints occur, automatic fallback to a verified quantized model variant with documented perf characteristics; customers may opt into a 30-day rollback.

5) Execution / next steps
- Attached: SOW-StrataVault-draft.pdf and pricing_grid_v2.xlsx.
- DocuSign link for our standard order form: https://redwood.app/docusign/abc123-sign (one-click sign will populate the negotiated credit language).

If this aligns, Procurement can sign via the DocuSign link; otherwise flag specific legal redlines and we will produce an annotated SOW. Happy to do a 30-min commercial committee walk-through Monday at 10am PT.

Best,
Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
